method: Four independent transparent reference-image editing calls, each using the exact identity plate AND its accepted V188 combat atlas. All four PNGs pass visual whole-body and read-only alpha/gutter inspection, then identical generated bytes are copied to the public paths. Measured variable rectangles, opaque support pixels and pelvis-projected airborne anchors are independently verified. Runtime simulation, animated loop captures and native player journeys are separate release checks. No Python drawing, repainting, alpha cleanup, resizing or pose synthesis is performed.
promptBase:
Create a NEW 2D game animation sprite sheet for the exact SAME organism shown in both supplied reference images: first is the identity master plate, second is the already accepted combat sprite atlas whose detailed retro sprite style, chitin palette, head shape and scale relationships must match. The new sheet is LOCOMOTION AND AIR ONLY, no attacks, KO or other creatures. EXACTLY TEN separately drawn full-body figures, one figure per cell, in a regular grid of FIVE columns by TWO rows, read left to right then top to bottom. Wide 5:2 canvas approximately 2560x1024. True transparent background with no baked checkerboard, no environment, floor, drop shadows, halos, labels, arrows, numbers, cell borders, text or guide lines. Keep at least 10% transparent padding around EVERY figure. All heads point RIGHT, tails trail LEFT. Every tail, fingertip, foot and head remains entirely inside its own cell; bend the long tail naturally to fit, never crop or shorten it. Use a constant pixel scale for the skull and body in all ten cells; never enlarge short or crouched poses to fill a cell. Preserve the exact single organism's recognizable proportions and bone/chitin detail from the references.

These are eight consecutive animation key drawings of ONE COMPLETE WALK CYCLE followed by two airborne joint poses. Make actual alternating limb articulation, not eight idle silhouettes, not eight whole-body rotations, not mirrored copies, not eight running leaps. The pelvis stays at a stable average x/y within its cell with only small natural vertical bob. In grounded poses, at least one supporting foot is planted at the same invisible ground plane near 90% of cell height; planted foot remains flat relative to that common line. Near and far limbs must exchange support halfway through the cycle. Repeated cell boundaries must not be touched.

TOP ROW:
1 WALK-0: first contact, NEAR support leg forward/heel or claws at contact and FAR support leg behind; opposite arm/forelimb reaches forward naturally.
2 WALK-1: down/compression after that contact, knees and elbows flex and body settles slightly; near support planted.
3 WALK-2: passing pose, near support bears the weight UNDER the pelvis while far moving leg passes it, lifted clear; opposing forelimb motion.
4 WALK-3: up/recovery, near support extends and far leg reaches toward its next forward contact; hips rise subtly, not a jump.
5 WALK-4: OPPOSITE contact from cell1, FAR leg forward at contact, NEAR leg behind; arm/forelimb support swapped.

BOTTOM ROW:
6 WALK-5: opposite down/compression, far support planted and body settles; distinct from cell2.
7 WALK-6: opposite passing, far support under pelvis and near moving leg lifted and passing; distinct from cell3.
8 WALK-7: opposite up/recovery approaching the first contact so looping 8 back to 1 is coherent; distinct from cell4.
9 AIR-RISE: airborne ascent, body slightly extended forward, knees/feet and forelimbs tucked freely off the invisible support line, tail counterbalances. Pelvis remains aligned with the same logical root as walking. No ground contact or jump effects.
10 AIR-FALL: airborne descent/landing anticipation, body prepares to absorb impact, feet and forelimbs extend down/forward while remaining above the invisible reference floor. Clearly different from air-rise. Same skull and anatomy scale, no contact shadow.

The airborne images describe JOINT POSES only; actual height above ground will be supplied by the game, so keep the logical pelvis/root consistent instead of drawing the whole creature high in its cell. Avoid standing-like air poses. For a quadruped, show a deliberate four-limb gait with the first support pattern swapped halfway through, not a bipedal redesign.

fidelity.reviewScope: Four recognizable project identities, ten separate new joint drawings each, eight articulated locomotion keys and two visibly free-limbed airborne poses. Primary orthographic, gait and motion timing references were not recovered.
remaining: Far limbs are partially occluded in some drawings; exact anatomical side assignment and canonical footfall timing are not certified.
The order is an original Tantalus game-animation interpretation; native loop evidence and runtime tests are recorded separately from this production provenance.
No authored special, super or paired-capture animation is added by these locomotion sheets.
These generated drawings do not certify 1:1 franchise anatomy, measured primary body ratios or source-game/film motion.

grid.rectangles: Measured independently by the atlas owner. The runtime data module is authoritative; proposed gutter cuts below are retained only as the initial read-only inspection.
grid.scale: One constant organism scale per sheet, derived from reviewed standing/walking anatomy; airborne poses must not be independently enlarged to fill cells.

alphaReview.technicalLimit: Read-only alpha inspection confirms complete outer silhouettes and per-row vertical cuts crossing alpha<=1 only; silhouette threshold16 remains explicit. Low-alpha gutter dust remains untouched, so a zero-alpha-gutter claim is not made.
